data.narrative:
Tokamak Energy is a Series C-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $335M+ to date. The broader nuclear energy sector comprises 11 comparable firms—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private, including Helion, X-Energy, and Valar Atomics—though a sufficiently tight peer cohort at identical stage and valuation tier does not yet exist for reliable median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis, the applicable triangulation method, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $335M total-raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $570M. This reflects typical venture capital step-up dynamics between Series C and subsequent rounds. Given data constraints, a range of $484M to $655M brackets this central estimate, representing ±15% sensitivity around the median.

The single-method reliance and absence of corroborating peer-median data constitute material uncertainty. Resolution would require either (i) closer identification of same-stage nuclear-energy private comparables with disclosed valuations, or (ii) granular revenue and EBITDA multiples from the public nuclear tickers. The $570M median valuation remains supportable as a Series C proxy but should be stress-tested against milestones (reactor demonstration timelines, regulatory approval pace) that would influence next-round pricing.
